description: Publish a versioned Slack collaboration Skill and inject its Server-owned reply context into Slack executions with integrity validation, initial/follow-up parity, non-Slack preservation, and fail-closed Runner behavior.

tasks.title: Publish the canonical versioned Slack collaboration Skill
tasks.description: Add the embedded Server Skill asset and catalog for `mohist-slack-collaboration` version `1.0.0`. Pin its version-to-content digest mapping so the catalog rejects embedded-byte drift, return the exact instruction body with its lowercase SHA-256 digest, and lock the six collaboration rules and the instruction-only reply-authorship boundary with asset contract tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolving the managed Skill returns the stable name `mohist-slack-collaboration`, version `1.0.0`, non-empty instructions, and a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the exact UTF-8 instruction bytes.

The published instructions explicitly cover all six Slack rules: useful content through the supplied send action, direct-question answers overriding silence, no empty acknowledgements, useful delegated callbacks and conditional mentions, self-contained conclusion/evidence/next-step replies with progress kept out of Slack, Server-provided reply-anchor use without destination guessing or internal-ID echoing, and silent recovery after restart, Session recovery, or compaction.

Asset contract tests verify the canonical rule content, stable identity, exact digest calculation, and that Runtime output, progress, or a missing Agent send action never becomes a Server-authored Slack reply; no question classifier or fallback response generator is introduced.

The Skill is resolved from the Server's embedded managed asset rather than a user filesystem or configurable Agent Skill; the catalog pins version `1.0.0` to digest `de3272639a1d390f3dcf915e65b6c057bf0b9eb91c51545572eb1e484c8c1a22`, rejects substituted or changed bytes under that version, and requires an explicit version/mapping change for new instructions.

Asset contract tests substitute the embedded body under the existing version and prove catalog resolution fails, while the Server asset and contract/unit test suite pass with no plaintext credentials, delivery-target selection, or changes to the existing Slack reply action ownership.
tasks.output: Embedded `mohist-slack-collaboration.skill.md`, Server Skill catalog and immutable identity/digest contract, plus passing Server asset contract tests.
tasks.notes: `docs/slack.md` remains the behavioral source of truth. Keep the Skill as managed execution input; do not add a new DSL or persist it into Agent definitions.

tasks.title: Deliver and enforce Slack execution context across Server and Runner
tasks.description: Implement the version-1 Server-created Slack execution context and wire it through both initial AgentJob launches and Slack follow-ups using a required durable `executionSource`, persisted effective thread roots, durable message provenance, and operation identities. Extend the Runner with one shared source/context validator and envelope path that injects the managed Skill and Server-provided anchor for Slack, rejects invalid contexts before enqueue or Runtime invocation, and leaves explicit non-Slack execution unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Every valid Slack direct-message initial launch, channel-root launch, and thread follow-up carries `executionSource: slack` and a complete version-1 context containing the published Skill snapshot and all reply-anchor fields: workspace, conversation, durable bound thread root, triggering message, initiating member, Connection, Session, and dispatch reference; non-Slack dispatches carry `executionSource: non-slack` and no Slack context.

Initial launches persist the source and complete context on the AgentJob input and copy both into the dispatch payload; they persist `threadTs ?? messageTs` as the bound root. Follow-ups derive the source, root, and representative message from durable Session/input provenance, preserve the root even for DM follow-ups with null incoming thread timestamps, use the follow-up operation as the dispatch identity, and fail construction rather than omit context when trusted origin, root, or provenance is incomplete.

Server contract/integration tests prove initial and follow-up parity for the persisted/published Skill name, version, exact instructions, and digest, while proving replay stability, correct DM/channel-root/thread anchors, deterministic first-input representative selection for batched follow-ups, and absence of secrets or Runtime-selected destinations.

The Runner's shared validator rejects an omitted or unknown `executionSource`, a `slack` source with omitted or null context, a `non-slack` source carrying context, a non-object or malformed context, unsupported context version, missing or empty anchor fields, missing or empty Skill fields, any identity other than the published `mohist-slack-collaboration` `1.0.0` Skill, non-canonical digest casing, and a digest that does not match the exact supplied UTF-8 instructions.

Validation runs at the control dispatcher and again at AgentJob and follow-up execution boundaries; omitted/null Slack contexts fail closed on both initial AgentJob and follow-up paths before Runtime selection/invocation or local follow-up enqueue, and are never treated as ordinary non-Slack work.

For valid Slack execution, the managed Skill is appended as execution-definition input and only `source: slack`, context version, and the Server-provided reply anchor are exposed as system facts; user text, Agent Instructions, configured Skills, and each input's prompt remain separate and the Agent cannot replace the anchor.

Web, CLI, Workflow, and other non-Slack launches and follow-ups carry the explicit `non-slack` source with no Slack context, retain their existing prompt, instructions, configured Skills, and envelope shape without Slack Skill, anchor, or Slack system facts, and do not require Slack validation.

Runner and Server tests cover modified Skill bodies, unsupported versions, incomplete/anchorless contexts, omitted/null contexts on both Slack initial and follow-up paths, explicit source/context mismatch rejection, initial/follow-up parity, DM bound-root preservation, multiple queued Slack inputs with deterministic representative anchoring, invalid follow-up no-enqueue, invalid AgentJob no-Runtime, non-Slack envelope preservation, and the unchanged Agent-owned Slack reply/delivery boundary; the relevant Server and Runner test suites pass.
tasks.output: Server `AgentSlackExecutionContext` contracts/factory, locked Skill resolution, durable source/root provenance, and initial/follow-up dispatch wiring; Runner source/context validation, managed Skill/system-facts envelope composition, fail-closed AgentJob/follow-up handling, and passing Server/Runner contract tests.
tasks.notes: Deploy Runner support before Server context emission. Persist source/root provenance as append-only dispatch/session state; keep the Skill out of long-lived Agent configuration and keep Slack delivery/outbox authorship with the existing Agent send action. For a batched turn, the first durable `InputId` is the only representative trigger; do not split the existing Session turn or guess a destination.
